title: The Faraday Bench
summary: Find magnetic flux and its change, then the emf induced in loops, coils and graphs of flux.
subject: physics
concepts: Induced emf in a loop in a solenoid
Average emf of a turning coil
learningOutcome: The student can find the flux through a coil and its change, and use the rate of change of flux to find the emf and current induced in loops, rotating coils and flux graphs.

levels.title: Flux through a coil
levels.adds: Baseline: Φ = BA cos θ, and the change in flux when the coil turns (Section 6.3).
hints: Φ = B A cos θ, with the area in m².
θ is the angle between the field and the normal to the coil.
A change is final minus initial, with its sign.

levels.title: Loop in a solenoid
levels.adds: New idea: the emf is the rate of change of flux, here μ₀nA ΔI/Δt (Ex 6.3).
hints: B = μ₀nI inside the solenoid, with n in turns per metre.
The flux through the loop is BA.
The emf is the change in flux divided by the time.

levels.title: Turning a coil
levels.adds: More steps: turning through 180° changes the flux by 2BA, for N turns (Example 6.3).
hints: Multiply by the number of turns.
The current is the emf over the resistance.

levels.title: Read the graph
levels.adds: Apply it: the emf is the slope of the flux graph, up or down (Section 6.4).
hints: Take the change in flux over the time in the segment.
The steepest segment has the largest emf, whichever way it slopes.

misconceptions: The emf depends on the flux itself, not on how fast it changes
A steady flux through a coil induces a steady emf
Turning a coil through 180° gives no change in flux
